title: Module 9 · Lesson 2 — Prompt injection and agent security

lines: Welcome to Module Nine, Lesson Two: prompt injection and agent security.
It's the defining agent threat, because agents read untrusted content and then act.
Picture a team whose coding agent reads code, runs tests, and pushes fixes.
Its shell holds the team's cloud keys.
One day it pulls in an open-source package.
Buried in a code comment is a note written for AI assistants, not people.
The agent obeys it and sends the keys to an outside server.
Nobody on the team did anything wrong.
That's indirect prompt injection, hidden in content the agent reads.
Unlike direct injection from the user, it hides in documents, web pages, tool results, or memory.
There's no complete fix, only layered containment.
First, treat all non-user content as data, never instructions.
Next, least privilege: only the tools it needs, with narrow, short-lived credentials.
An agent that never holds the cloud keys can't leak them.
Authorise every call server-side, under the user's identity.
A hijacked agent then can't exceed that user's rights, defeating the confused deputy.
Require human approval for irreversible, high-impact actions.
It holds even when everything upstream fails.
Rails screen inputs and retrieved content for injection, and outputs for leaks.
Egress control limits which hosts tools can reach.
Finally, monitor tool sequences.
A sudden network call right after reading a package is a red flag.
Excessive agency means too many permissions, so split read from write.
And never pass tool output into a shell or query unsanitised.
Agent-written code runs in a sandbox, like a container or microVM.
No ambient credentials, capped resources, and restricted network.
Denial of wallet drives costly loops, so set rate limits and budgets.
Memory poisoning fires later, so sanitise on write and distrust memory on read.
The exam trap: a system-prompt line telling the model to ignore injected instructions.
Prompts are defaults attackers can talk over, so enforce in the runtime, and read on.
